dossier.public_summary: About a 4 Earth-radius flat-bottom dip repeats every 14.4 days on a small M dwarf star with no odd-even or secondary eclipse and a duration that matches the star, favouring a planet interpretation. Individual transits scatter more than expected but the two-year average depth is steady and the shape is planetary. Higher-precision photometry and a definitive location check would confirm the planet and explain the scatter.

reasons.why: Strong flat-bottom preference (negative v_sigma) favours a planetary transit over a V-shaped grazing EB, consistent with fit_b 0.09507 and rp_rearth 3.722

Planet-sized for a 0.3894 Rsun M dwarf, no odd/even difference (diff_sigma 0.88, depth ratio 1.2) and no significant secondary (snr 3.218 < 5, well below best_brightening_snr 3.436). Duration ratio 1.262 (observed 3 h vs central 2.378 h) fits the star, confirmed by FLAME radii giving ratio 1.15 and rp 4.07-4.11 Rearth.

Sectors p_constant 0.03353 nominally low but tool returns steady across only 2 TESS-SPOC sectors (depths 8854 +/-1099 ppm vs 5745 +/-966 ppm not significant), so alone is not evidence for variability. Centroid is inconclusive (no clear difference image) so no off-target evidence, but neighbours.plausible_within_1px 1 only needs a 25% eclipse and contratio 0.008369 is low; flat bottom, duration and size together positively favour the target.

Individual transits are formally inconsistent (p 4.0e-09, depths 1610 ppm at -4.3 sigma and 13002 ppm at +4.0 sigma, share_of_top_3 0.989) but the star shows spot variability and only 4 transits; sector-averaged depth is stable (steady verdict) arguing against a few bad events dominating a false alarm, though low SNR refit 10.53 supports caution.
